highlights: THE PLANE OF SKY TAB SHOWS YOUR QUESTS AGAIN, ONE PER REWARD (discussion #184, thanks bjstrange). Folding the widget's Sky card into the Quest Tracker last release re-grouped the tab by the TURN-IN NPC - and one NPC hands out every sky reward for a class, so all fourteen landed in a single undifferentiated list and "which pieces does this one still need" stopped being answerable. Rows now group by the reward you're working toward, each with its own count and a ready / in progress / done note, and the heading opens that quest's wiki page. Your ticks are untouched; only the arrangement changed.

AND EVERY ROW NAMES WHERE THE ITEM DROPS AGAIN (same report). "Isle 3: Gorgalosk" was sitting in EQBuddy's own data the whole time and simply wasn't being drawn - the old card showed it, the new tab didn't. The turn-in NPC and the drop location are both back, on every row, on Windows, Linux and macOS.

A MIS-CLICKED TICK CAN BE TAKEN BACK (same report - bjstrange lost three and had to work out from memory what had been checked). Ticking a checklist row saves immediately and said nothing, so a stray click was unrecoverable. A bar now names what just changed and offers ↶ undo, Ctrl+Z works too, and it steps back through as many as you need.

ITEMS EQBUDDY TICKED FOR YOU ARE MARKED (same report: "all are checked with no indication of anything needing manual adjustments"). When several classes want the same drop, the loot auto-tick has to pick one and can't know which of yours earned it - so it picks and flags the row. EQBuddy Mobile has been showing that * for months; both desktop builds were quietly drawing a bare tick. They now show it too, with a tooltip saying why, and moving the tick settles it.

THE CLASS FILTER STOPS EATING THE WINDOW when you tick more than a few classes. Selecting all sixteen turned the button into "BRD · BST · BER · CLR · DRU · ENC · MAG · MNK · NEC · PAL · RNG · ROG · SHD · SHM · WAR · WIZ", which pushed the mine/zone/held/done/all strip clean off the edge, and the chip row beside it was clipped mid-list. The button now reads "All classes" or "7 classes" past three (hover for the full list), and the chips wrap onto a second line.

FIXED (discussion #186, thanks Kemble-Kemble) - THE QUEST TRACKER WAS CUT OFF ON A SECOND MONITOR AND COULDN'T BE SHRUNK. Its height was capped against your PRIMARY screen, so dragging it to a smaller one left it taller than that screen with no way back. The cap now follows whichever monitor the window is actually on, and re-applies as you drag it between them. Ctrl + mouse wheel also resizes the window itself now rather than only the text inside it - that shortcut works on every EQBuddy window and is worth knowing.

FIXED (discussion #193, thanks wizen) - THE SKY AND EPIC CHECKLISTS TICKED ITEMS YOU NEVER LOOTED, sometimes for a dozen classes at once. When several classes want the same drop, EQBuddy is supposed to tick only the classes you actually play. With no class filter set, an empty class selection was being read as "every class matches" rather than "no class matches" - so ONE Wind Rune Azia ticked the Druid, Monk and Wizard tests together, and one Red Dragon Scales ticked both the Bard and Warrior epics. This became permanent in 1.88.0: the widget's old Sky and Epic cards used to keep a class selected, and when those cards folded into the Quest Tracker nothing set it any more. A shared drop with no class to attribute it to now ticks ONCE and wears a * for you to move, which is what it always did when a filter was set. If your checklists were already over-ticked, the fix stops it happening again but cannot know which ticks were wrong - set your classes in the Quest Tracker's class picker, then correct the rows; sorry for the tidying.

AND YOUR CLASS PICK NOW ACTUALLY DRIVES IT. Setting your class(es) in the Quest Tracker was always the intended way to scope these ticks, and it is now the ONLY thing that does - so it is worth setting even if you only play one character.

FIXED, FIFTH TIME (discussion #135, thanks bjstrange, who has now sent six logs) - CHARM STILL DIDN'T ALWAYS REPORT HOW LONG IT HELD. charm6.txt is a 3:28 charm on the Plane of Sky that announced its fade with no duration, and the cause is a new one again. He charmed Bzzazzt, put the pet on hold, and eight seconds later "Bzzazzt" landed a full five-hit round on him - so EQBuddy read that as his pet turning on him and threw the clock away fifteen seconds in. There were TWO Bzzazzt. The same-name guard added in 1.87.0 couldn't help, because the only proof it accepts is a creature attacking something with its own name, and these two never fought each other: the charmed one was busy with Eye of Veeshan (it killed it), the other was busy with him. But his pet had already said the thing that settles it - "Now holding, Master. I will not start attacks until ordered." A pet on hold does not start attacks, so a same-named attacker while yours is held is a different creature, and the claim now survives until the wear-off line settles it. Releasing the hold gives the ordinary rule back, and a nearby charmer's pet answering THEIR hold order is ignored. Verified by replaying his actual file: 'held 3:28', against no duration at all before.

FIXED (discussion #183, thanks TheLethean) - WAKING ONE MEZZED MOB COULD CLEAR THE CHIPS FOR ITS SAME-NAMED NEIGHBOURS. Waking a mob prints TWO lines - "Your Mesmerization spell has worn off of a skeleton." and "A skeleton has been awakened by Dorr." - and EQBuddy was dropping a chip for each, so every wake cost two. With a stack of identically-named mobs that reads exactly as "they all disappeared". The two lines are one break and are now paired: whichever arrives first drops the chip, the other is recognised as its partner. Order-proof, because his log prints the fade FIRST, which is why the existing guard never saw it. Two mobs genuinely broken at once still print two of each line, so both still count. His second log - which counts the losses per wake precisely - is what made this findable; a differently-named mob was never affected, and that detail is what proved it was name-scoped.

THE RESPAWN TIMER FINDS NAMED MOBS THE CATALOG HAS NEVER HEARD OF (discussion #185, thanks elderbit). Camping Focus Items he hit the gaps a hand-maintained list will always have — almost every named in The Hole, Chief Goonda in Western Karana - and pointed out that the log already tells us: EverQuest writes trash with an article ("an ogre shaman") and a named by its proper name ("Chief Goonda"). EQBuddy now reads that. Kill a proper-named mob that isn't in the catalog and it starts tracking it - with NO countdown, because one kill cannot know the cycle; the second kill measures it, and later shorter gaps tighten it. The row says "Found by EQBuddy" so you can tell it apart from the catalog and from your own entries, and you can type a duration over it or remove it.

IT IS DELIBERATELY CAUTIOUS, because an invented timer sends you to a camp that isn't up. Only YOUR OWN kills count - which is also what keeps pets and players out, the case elderbit flagged himself: they die as "X has been slain by Y", never as "You have slain X!". Gaps under 90 seconds and over six hours teach nothing. And his convention has one real exception we already knew about: Solusek's Eye's trash clockworks are called "CWG Model XA" with no article at all. Where the catalog lists a family's named (CWG Model EXG), that is a statement that its siblings are trash, and they are left alone - the same family rule that stopped them hijacking his clock in 1.88.3. The shipped catalog is still only ever edited by hand; discoveries live with your own learned timers.

QUEST REWARDS WRITTEN AS A TABLE COUNT AS REWARDS. The wiki reformatted the Soldier's Brooch page from a bullet list into a stat-comparison table, and this week's catalog refresh promoted the quest with an empty reward list - all eight class brooches gone. Our reader stopped at the table's first "=" sign. Fixed at the source and re-harvested.
EQBuddy is a BETA - if something reads wrong, tell us: ⚙ → Help → Send feedback.

THE WIDGET CAN FLOAT OVER FULLSCREEN EVERQUEST ON A MAC (thanks Liminal Warmth). Running EQBuddy under CrossOver, a fullscreen game painted straight over the widget - you played windowed or you didn't see EQBuddy. That's a Wine-on-macOS quirk rather than an EQBuddy bug: Wine hands a fullscreen game a window level no ordinary always-on-top window can beat. There's now an opt-in overlay mode that floats the widget over the game and stops a click on it pulling the game out of the foreground. It needs a one-time patch to Wine's Mac driver - see docs/CrossOver-macOS-overlay.md - and it is off by default and completely inert on Windows. The setup script builds that patch on your own machine from CodeWeavers' published source: we deliberately ship no prebuilt binary, because the step replaces a library inside your CrossOver install and you shouldn't have to trust an unreadable file from us to do it.

SPAWN TIMERS NO LONGER "LEARN" A RESPAWN FROM TWO DIFFERENT MOBS (thanks Liminal Warmth). In Solusek's Eye, killing an ordinary clockwork could start CWG Model EXG's 18-minute countdown - the typo-forgiving matcher bridged the whole CWG Model XA/XB/XC serial family onto the named - and then killing the REAL EXG at the bridge 93 seconds later taught EQBuddy that his respawn is 93 seconds, permanently. That gap was walk time between two different mobs, not a spawn cycle. The matcher now refuses name-family siblings (a shared name with a different last word is another mob, not a typo), and a countdown only learns from the named's own kills on both ends of a gap - placeholder kills still restart the clock, they just can't teach it a duration. The ▶ manual start also always takes effect now, even backdated behind a running timer. If a named of yours got stuck with an absurdly short timer, clear its duration in the Spawns window once to return to the catalog value.

FIXED (discussion #173, thanks KoboldCoterie again) - THE TITLE BAR COULD STAND YOUR CHARACTER'S NAME UP VERTICALLY, one letter per line, on Linux. Reserving room for the CPU/memory readout in 1.88.0 left the name too little space, and the name label wrapped instead of shortening - so a widget that had just stopped resizing itself started spelling K-o-b-o-l-d downwards in a title bar three times too tall. The name now stays on one line and ends in an ellipsis when it doesn't fit, which is what it should always have done. The keyboard fix he confirmed is unaffected.

CHARM PETS ARE CLAIMED MORE ACCURATELY - AND FEWER PETS THAT AREN'T YOURS (thanks chrstahl, discussion #177). When you charm something, the "it's yours now" line arrives about one cast time later, so EQBuddy now waits exactly that long PER SPELL: nine seconds for Cajole Undead, under four for Charm. One fixed wait could never fit both. Which spells are charms, and how long each takes, now comes straight from the wiki and refreshes weekly - so a new charm, or a corrected cast time, reaches you without anyone typing it in. That list is built from what each spell DOES rather than what it is called, which turned up a real culprit: Allure of Death - a necromancer mana regen - was being treated as a charm purely because of its name, so casting it could hand you a nearby enchanter's pet and credit its damage to you for as long as that pet lived. Four other innocently-named spells were doing the same. Bards also gain Solon's Bravura and Tunare's Request being recognised under both the spellings the game and the wiki use.

/PET WHO LEADER NOW SETTLES IT EITHER WAY (chrstahl's own suggestion). Ask your pet who its leader is and the answer is final: name you, and that pet is yours from that moment. Name somebody else - a nearby player's pet answering their question - and EQBuddy lets go of it. That is the only way to correct a pet it guessed wrong about while the guess is still costing you an accurate number, and it is worth putting on your charm macro or a hotkey if pet damage matters to you.

POTION BUFFS SHOW ON THE BUFF TRACKER (issue #167, thanks Liminal Warmth). Drinking a Distillate of Alacrity or Clarity never produced a timer: the potions cast Elixir spells that had no wiki page, and the buff catalog is harvested from the wiki. The whole alchemy catalog is now documented there and absorbed here - roughly 50 potion buffs join the tracker (every Distillate line, the Awareness focus potions, Turtle's Drink, the racial essences and more), and their fade lines are recognized so a chip clears the moment the buff actually drops instead of lingering at 0:00.

THE QUEST TRACKER HAS ONE WAY IN NOW. Type what you actually know - the REWARD you want ("Wakizashi of the Frozen Skies"), an item in your bags, the quest's name, the NPC who gives it, or a zone - and the quest comes back, with 📌 to keep tracking it. That search already worked, but it sat under a "+ I have this" item-and-quantity row that won the eye completely; David missed the search entirely for weeks. The row is gone and the box now says what it takes.

AND A ⧉ SCAN BAGS BUTTON replaces what that row was for. Rather than typing in items you owned before EQBuddy could see them - spelling and all - copy /outputfile inventory, paste it in the game's chat, and EQBuddy reads your bags AND your bank exactly. The held tab then shows every quest you could hand in right now. Same one-click ⧉ contract as the Gear Locker and the Raids card.

FIXED - THE EQBUDDY MOBILE QR CODE COULD POINT AT AN ADDRESS YOUR PHONE CAN'T REACH. If your PC has Tailscale, Hyper-V, VirtualBox or WSL, those adapters have addresses that look exactly as private as your real Wi-Fi, and whichever one Windows happened to list first won the QR - so the scan just timed out, which looks like a firewall problem and isn't. EQBuddy now prefers the adapter that actually has a route to the internet, which is the one your tablet is on. If pairing has been failing for you, this is why.

SEARCHING THE QUEST TRACKER NO LONGER FREEZES IT. Typing rebuilt the whole list on every single keystroke, and with the full 1,172-quest catalog in view that meant nine rebuilds for a word like "Wakizashi" - the window appeared to hang. It now waits for you to stop typing, and shows the first 60 matches with a "+N more" line rather than laying out hundreds of cards you'd never scroll to.

ONE QUESTS CARD ON THE WIDGET, IN PLACE OF "Sky Quest" AND "Epics". Both of those cards carried a full tabbed checklist on the widget itself - fourteen class tabs, a search box, state filters - which is a lot of screen for something you read between pulls rather than during one. They are now a single "Quests" card that opens the Quest Tracker window, where all three tabs already live. The card still shows both scores at a glance ("Epic 1/12 · Sky 3/40"), your checklists still tick themselves as you loot with nothing open at all, and "Quest tracker…" has left the ⚙ menu because the card is the way in. If you had hidden both old cards, the new one starts hidden too; if you had either one showing, it shows. The Epic tab's "classic-doable only" filter moved into the Quest Tracker with it.

EQBUDDY MOBILE GETS THE WHOLE QUEST TRACKER. One "Quests" screen on your tablet or mobile device now carries the same three tabs as the PC window - Quests, Epic 1.0, Plane of Sky - with the same search box (rewards, items, quest names, NPCs, zones), the class chips and the full class picker on every tab, and the same cards: progress per turn-in item, ✔ ready, the wiki link. Tap 📌 to track a quest, tap Epic and Sky rows to tick them - every tap lands in the same place a desktop click does, so both screens always agree. Search runs ON the device: the PC sends the whole quest catalog once, so typing costs no round trips and answers as fast as the desktop does. The separate Epic-checklist and Sky-checklist screens folded into this one; a device that was showing them keeps its pick under the new name automatically.

FIXED, FOURTH TIME LUCKY (discussion #135, thanks bjstrange, who has now sent five logs) - CHARM STILL DIDN'T ALWAYS REPORT HOW LONG IT HELD. His latest log shows a 5-minute charm that announced its fade with no duration, and the cause is one nobody had considered: the creature had cast a damage-over-time spell (Choking) on him BEFORE he charmed it, and that spell kept ticking afterwards. EQBuddy read each tick as "my pet just turned on me", threw the clock away six seconds into the charm, and the real fade five minutes later had no landing left to measure. A tick is not a decision to attack - it is the tail of a spell cast before the charm existed - so ticks no longer break a charm. Genuine swings still do. This is why the previous three fixes missed it: all of them key on a real attack, and this charm ended with no attack at all. The mez tracker had already learned this exact lesson back in issue #32; charm never got the same guard.

FIXED ON LINUX AND macOS (discussion #169, thanks joma65) - YOUR WINDOWS CAME BACK AT THE TOP-LEFT CORNER every launch: the main widget, the spawns window and both chip stacks, all at 0,0 however carefully you had parked them. When a window closes, X11 and Wayland can report its position as 0,0 while it is being torn down - and EQBuddy wrote that number down as though you had dragged the window there. The two chip stacks already defended against this; the other windows did not, and the same trap catches a window OPENING too, because the desktop applies a move a moment after it is asked for. EQBuddy now records only a position it saw while the window was genuinely on screen, and if it never saw one it leaves your saved spot alone. Windows was never affected. If your positions were already flattened, they are yours to set once more - this stops them being lost again.

FIXED (discussion #169, thanks joma65) - LINUX AND macOS RAN A WHOLE SECOND COPY OF EQBUDDY EVERY TIME YOU LAUNCHED IT. Only the Windows build stopped a second copy starting; everywhere else every launch started another one, and because two widgets are undecorated, always on top, and restore to the same saved spot, they sat exactly on top of each other and looked like one. Each copy loads all your settings at startup and writes all of them back on any change, so whichever one saved last quietly reverted everything the other had changed - the likely reason the two "hide the widget" tick-boxes wouldn't stay ticked, while your window positions (identical in both copies) appeared to hold. Launching EQBuddy again now brings the running one to the front instead, on every platform, and a leftover lock file can never stop it starting. EQBuddy also records in error.log when something else changes settings.json underneath it, so this can never hide again.

FIXED (discussion #173, thanks KoboldCoterie) - ON LINUX, TURNING ON THE TITLE-BAR CPU/MEMORY READOUT COULD STOP THE KEYBOARD REACHING EVERQUEST. The readout's text got wider as the numbers grew, and because the widget sizes itself to its contents, every refresh resized a real always-on-top window - every three seconds, forever, whether or not anything else had changed. Over a fullscreen game on X11 that is enough to disturb it, and the reported symptom was exactly that: the mouse kept working and the keyboard stopped. The readout now reserves a fixed width and formats to a fixed shape, so a new sample repaints and nothing else. Nothing was wrong with the measurement itself and the numbers are unchanged. Windows was never affected, but it carried the same growing-text code and now shares the fixed one.

FIXED (discussion #120, thanks Frankthetankk) - CLASS DETECTION WORKS BOTH WAYS NOW. EQBuddy guesses your class from the log when you haven't picked one, and it knew only MELEE skills - so a caster who once produced a melee-ish line wore that class for the rest of the session, and nothing he did afterwards could argue back, because there was nothing in the table a caster could ever trigger. All sixteen classes can now produce evidence, drawn from the spell and AA catalogs EQBuddy already ships rather than a hand-typed list. Recent play outweighs what you were doing an hour ago, so swapping characters converges on the one you're actually playing. Where an item could have cast the spell it wants to see two different ones, so a borrowed clicky can't flip you the other way. And when the log is genuinely ambiguous it now says nothing instead of guessing - it was always labelled "(inferred)", and an honest blank is better than a confident wrong answer. This also fixes Shadow Knight and Paladin never being detected by Harm Touch or Lay on Hands, which print as spell damage and so missed the melee-only check entirely.

FIXED (discussion #175, thanks jlcrisp) - BEASTLORD WAS MISSING FROM EVERY CLASS PICKER. He spotted it on the buff-set picker, but one list feeds them all, so Beastlord was equally absent from the quest tracker, the Plane of Sky tab, the buff breakout and EQBuddy Mobile. The wiki is clear that Legends has sixteen classes; our list had fifteen, and it looks to have been read off the epic roster - Beastlord has no Epic 1.0, which is correct rather than an omission. It does have five Plane of Sky tests, and it now appears everywhere it should, abbreviated BST as the wiki writes it.

FIXED (discussion #176, thanks Fennec-Halas) - THE PALADIN GOLDEN HILT POINTED AT THE WRONG ISLE. EQBuddy sent you to Isle 2 and the Protector of Sky for Thelvorn, Blade of Light; it actually drops from the sphinxes, drakes and undine spirits on ISLE 7. Checked four ways against the wiki before changing it, including that Isle 2's boss drop list contains no Golden Hilt at all. Note the wiki's own Golden Hilt page still labels its quest link "Paladin Test of Compassion" when the quest is Paladin Test of Love - the link goes to the right page, only the label is wrong.

MOTES ARE WEIGHED, NOT JUST COUNTED (discussion #154, thanks EzraSmith). The Motes card now reports the upgrade experience your session's motes are actually worth, because a hundred Infinitesimal motes and a hundred Infinite ones are not the same hour. Checking the wiki's table to build it turned up two errors of our own that counting had hidden: we had Major and Greater the wrong way round, and we ranked the plain "Mote of Potential" at the bottom of the ladder when it is the fourth rung and worth 4. Void-Touched Potential is recognised too - it counts, and weighs nothing, because it raises a whole tier instead of adding experience.

FIXED (issue #153, thanks adndmike) - THE ALERT VOLUME SLIDER DID NOTHING TO YOUR OWN .WAV FILES, while it moved the seven built-in sounds perfectly. The slider was never the problem: your sound wasn't playing at all. If EQBuddy couldn't find the file you had picked - moved, renamed, on a drive that wasn't plugged in - it quietly played the Windows notification ding instead, and that one comes from Windows at Windows' volume, so 10% and 100% sounded identical. The built-ins ship with Windows and are always there, which is why they alone appeared to obey the slider. There is now no route left that the slider can't reach: a sound that has gone missing gets a banner naming the file, and Ding stands in at YOUR volume until you pick another. Same fix on Linux and macOS, where the fall-through was a console beep.

STILL OPEN in the same report: the two "hide the widget while the game isn't focused / isn't running" tick-boxes also came back off, and that has a different cause which we have not found yet. Nothing in the code turns them off, so we would rather say so than ship a guess. If this is happening to you, your ~/.config/EQBuddy/error.log is the thing that will crack it.

FIXED AGAIN (discussion #135, thanks bjstrange for a fourth log) - CHARM STILL LOST ITS HELD TIME when two creatures share a name. His log says it outright: "A greater ice bones slashes a greater ice bones." Your charmed one was fighting the uncharmed one, and the UNCHARMED one was hitting you - EQ's log identifies creatures only by name, so EQBuddy could not tell them apart and read it as your pet turning on you. The claim was dropped six seconds into a 32-second charm, so the fade had nothing left to measure. A pet that is demonstrably busy hitting something else no longer loses its claim to a same-named attacker; the wear-off line settles it instead. This is a different cause from the in-flight-swing fix in 1.85.0, which is why that one did not cover it.

FIXED (discussion #120, thanks Frankthetankk - who found this AND fixed it at the source) - SYMBOL OF PINZARN ALWAYS READ AS MISSING, however many times you cast it. EQBuddy watches for the exact text a buff prints when it lands, and the wiki had the wrong text on file for this one - so it was waiting for a line your log never contains. He corrected the wiki page; EQBuddy now has the real message and a 45-minute timer to go with it. Endure Magic, Poison, Disease, Cold and Fire also became trackable in 1.86.0, if you had been unable to add those.

FIXED (discussion #172, thanks bjstrange) - UNCHECKING A SKY QUEST ITEM LEFT THE QUEST LOOKING READY. Ticking the last item marks a quest ready to turn in; unticking it again updated the counters but not the list itself, so the ready label stayed put until something else forced a redraw. The list now refreshes exactly when a quest's readiness changes - and not on every tick, so checking off a long quest no longer loses your scroll position.

FORAGED ITEMS COUNT NOW (discussion #163, thanks wizen). The game announces a forage as "You have scrounged up ..." rather than a normal loot line, and EQBuddy was ignoring it entirely. Forages now appear on the Loot card and in the new recent-drops view with "Forage" as their source, which also means a foraged item can tick a quest or gear row like any other. A failed forage is still ignored - a miss is not a drop.
EQBuddy is a BETA - if something reads wrong, tell us: ⚙ → Help → Send feedback.

BUFF TIMERS NAME THE SPELL LINE INSTEAD OF QUOTING THE GAME (discussion #162, thanks DeusSilvam). A tracked buff used to be labelled with whatever the game printed - "You feel much faster" - while other lines already showed a proper name. 37 of the 163 tracked lines were like that; they now read "Haste line", "Cleric AC line", "Thorns damage shield", "Levitation" and so on. Nothing you have configured moves: these are display names only.

42 MORE BUFFS CAN BE TIMED (discussion #162, thanks DeusSilvam, who noticed his shaman spells were missing). Talisman of Altuna, Strength, Agility, Dexterity, Stamina and Spirit of the Puma are now tracked, along with 36 others - the Endure/Resist lines, Charisma, Health, Nimble, Feet like Cat and more. They were absent because the wiki leaves the "beneficial" field blank on some pages and EQBuddy read silence as "not a buff"; a blank now qualifies when the spell targets a friend or yourself AND the page calls it a buff, which keeps debuffs out.

A WAY BACK IF AN UPDATE GOES WRONG (discussion #158, thanks n3cr0nk1tt3n for the idea and twidget76 for the report that prompted it). EQBuddy's updater lives inside the widget, so a build that won't start takes the route to its own fix with it - which is exactly what happened with 1.84.0. From now on the installer keeps the build it replaces, and adds a Start-menu shortcut "EQBuddy (previous version)". If an update ever leaves you with a widget that won't open, start that one instead and update from inside it. It appears only once there is a previous build to go back to, and uninstalling removes it.

THE LOOT CARD CAN SHOW EVERY DROP AS IT HAPPENED (discussion #160, thanks wizen). The sort row on the Loot card gains a third option, "recent": your session's raw loot in arrival order, newest first, instead of totals. It exists for long farms - when you have looted 200 HQ Lion Skins, a rare pelt appearing is a count going from 0 to 1, which looks exactly like the skin count going from 200 to 201. In arrival order it is simply the row that is not a Lion Skin. Runs of the same item collapse into one line with a count, so a streak cannot push the interesting drop off the end.

BUFF LOSSES CAN NAME A DEBUFF AS THE CAUSE (discussion #120, thanks Frankthetankk). The lost-buff history could already say "lost as X landed" when a nuke or a slow displaced one of your set buffs - but a PURE debuff deals no damage and is not a slow, so it landed in total silence and the buff it displaced was recorded as merely "faded". 615 detrimental spells now have their cast-on-you lines catalogued, so his documented case reads "lost as Malaise landed" instead. The window is deliberately tight and a shared line names every candidate rather than guessing one - a wrong cause in a bug report to the game devs is worse than no cause.

FIXED, AND THE REASON TO UPDATE (discussion #158, thanks twidget76) - EQBUDDY 1.84.0 WOULD NOT START if you had the Epic card's "classic-doable only" filter ticked. It appeared in Task Manager using no CPU, never reached the taskbar, and never opened a window - and because the failed launch left a process behind, a second double-click did nothing either. Restoring that checkbox at startup called into a part of the app that had not been built yet, which was a mistake introduced by 1.84.0's internal reorganisation of the quest checklists. If this hit you, nothing was damaged: your settings, history and logs were untouched the whole time. An automated launch test now runs with that filter ON, because the reason this reached anyone is that the old test only covered it OFF.

FIXED (discussion #135, thanks bjstrange, whose log finally cracked it) - CHARM SOMETIMES DIDN'T REPORT HOW LONG IT HELD. If the creature was mid-swing at the instant your charm landed, the game resolved that attack round anyway - and EQBuddy read your brand-new pet hitting you as the charm breaking, throwing away the clock one second after starting it. Minutes later the real fade had nothing left to measure, so the "held M:SS" went missing while the fade message itself printed as normal. That is why it looked random and moved between mobs: it depended entirely on the creature's swing timer. A hit within 3 seconds of the landing is now the tail of that round rather than a break.

FIXED (discussion #156, thanks bjstrange) - UPGRADED DROPS NOW TICK SKY ROWS. "Azure Ring +1" is an Azure Ring, but the Sky checklist compared the name exactly while the Epic and Gear checkers both folded the "+N" away - so one loot line ticked a gear wish and an epic step and silently skipped the Sky row that wanted the same item. Note this only applies to loot as it arrives; tick anything you already have by hand once.

FIXED (discussion #120, thanks Frankthetankk) - A BUFF ADDED UNDER A CLASS YOU AREN'T PLAYING VANISHED. Picking, say, Paladin in the buff-set class picker and clicking a searched buff appeared to do nothing - and then the buff disappeared from later searches, so you couldn't even retry. It was being added correctly every time; the breakout just never showed buckets outside your active classes, so the pick was stored, hidden and unremovable. Those picks were never lost and now appear as a parked section. Options and the breakout share one answer about this now.

FIXED (discussion #144, thanks n3cr0nk1tt3n) - THE BOTTOM CARD COULD BE CUT OFF with no way to scroll to the rest of it, and whether it happened depended on your widget size slider - the Epics card showed it first, being the longest. The card list lives under the size transform, so the limit it gets is measured in different units than the screen figure it was being handed; the two only agreed at 100%. Away from that, the list's idea of its own room drifted from what the window could show, and once it thought it had more room than existed the last card was simply clipped. NEW - EQBUDDY NOW RENDERS UNDER WINE (PR #148, contributed by liminalwarmth - this one is entirely their work): players running the Windows build through Wine on Linux or CrossOver on macOS got empty boxes instead of every icon. Wine prefixes ship no Segoe fonts, and Wine's text engine only ever looks at the app's PRIMARY font - so EQBuddy now bundles one font containing everything it draws, text and icons alike, and switches to it only when it detects Wine. On real Windows nothing changes at all. They also added a test that fails the build if anyone adds an icon the bundled font doesn't cover, so it can't quietly rot.

NEW - EQBUDDY MOBILE (BETA) IS OUT OF PREVIEW: put EQBuddy on the phone or tablet already sitting beside your keyboard. Click the 📱 button in the title bar, scan the code with the device's camera, and its browser becomes a second screen - a live zone map, spawn timers, mez chips, buffs, combat breakdowns, session stats, loot, XP, and your Epic/Sky/Gear checklists. Each device picks WHICH of those it shows and in what order, so the tablet propped up beside you and the phone in your pocket can show completely different things. Nothing to install on the device, and it updates with EQBuddy itself.

It is OFF until you turn it on, and it stays on your own Wi-Fi. No account, no cloud, no telemetry: the pages are served by EQBuddy.exe straight to your device, and nothing leaves your network. You decide what may be sent at all (Options → Behavior → EQBuddy Mobile), and "New code" instantly locks out every device you have paired.

Worth knowing up front: Windows will ask to allow EQBuddy through the firewall the first time you switch it on - if you dismiss that prompt, devices simply can't connect and nothing will say why, so switch it off and on again to get the prompt back. Guest/public Wi-Fi that isolates devices from each other will also block it. And browsers won't hold a screen awake over plain HTTP, so bump your device's screen timeout if you're camping.

NEW - THE MOBILE MAP NOW MATCHES THE PC'S: your /loc breadcrumb trail (the comet tail that fades over the last minute of movement), camp pins for every named you're waiting on - marked "~" when the location came from the wiki rather than your own kill - and the full Named list beside the map with countdowns and elapsed bars. FIXED (issue #116, thanks Fennec-Halas): bards no longer get a false 🐌 slow alert when Selo's Accelerando fades — "You slow down." is both a real slow's landing line AND how Selo's haste wears off, and EQBuddy now reads the "You forget…" line to tell them apart. NEW: a system tray icon, always present while EQBuddy runs (#114 follow-up, thanks Frankthetankk) — when the widget hides itself, the tray icon is how you see it's alive and click it back. Windows tucks new tray icons behind the ^ chevron; drag it out if you want it always visible.

NEW (discussion #94, Frankthetankk's field report): 🐌 chips now show counter type and count on their face — "Slowed 40% · disease 12" — and the chip stack can be parked BEFORE you're ever slowed: open Options and an empty stack shows a draggable "drag me" placeholder.

NEW (discussion #106, bjstrange's rule, built as spoken): a Sky item that several classes want but none of your filtered classes claim now ticks the first owning class with a * marker — hover it to see who else wants the item, and move the tick if the guess was wrong. Touching the checkbox clears the *.

NEW — Gear checklist (first outside code contribution to a card, thanks dandrews2930!): build a shopping list on eqlegendstools.com's character sheet, Export Shopping List, then Options → Cards & windows → "Import gear list…" — the 🛡 Gear card shows every slot's target item with sources and a checkbox. NEW (discussion #114, thanks Frankthetankk): Options → Behavior → "Hide the widget while the game isn't running at all" — the overlay exists only while you play. Distinct from hide-when-unfocused (which keeps the widget up between sessions); they compose. Need it back without the game? Launch EQBuddy again — the running copy surfaces while you use it.

NEW (discussion #112, thanks Frankthetankk): Options → Behavior → "Show EQBuddy's own CPU & memory in the title bar" — a small dim readout ("0.3% · 84 MB", refreshed every few seconds, CPU as a share of ALL cores) so you can hold the widget accountable. Off by default; diagnostics aren't furniture.

Under the hood, a tuning pass to keep that number honest: the fight timeline no longer rebuilds its data every second when nothing happened, the chip stack stopped assembling itself twice a second just to learn it was empty, and the Buffs card updates its clocks in place instead of rebuilding rows every tick. FIXED (David's field report): expanding a card could sit empty for seconds — sections only redrew on new log events or a 10-second heartbeat, so a click during a quiet moment waited for one. Expanding now renders immediately. NEW: Sky Quest search (discussion #108, thanks bjstrange — his third shipped ask this week): type an item or reward name in the box next to the state filter and every class's matching rows appear at once, live checkboxes included — no more touring fourteen tabs to find who wants your drop. Search crosses all classes and ignores the state lens, same rule as the quest tracker: filters shape tabs, never search. Clear the box and the tabs return.

The fight timeline earns its space (David's pass on a real fight): the window now OPENS fitted to the fight — a five-skill skirmish opens compact, a raid brawl opens tall — and stays fully resizable; lanes stretch to fill whatever size you choose instead of huddling at the top. Lane totals say what they are ("619 dmg", "217 taken"), a legend line explains the marks, the DPS graph grew a scale and a series key, and miss/resist outlines went neutral gray — orange now means exactly one thing: critical.

FIXED (discussion #106, thanks bjstrange — five days after his #98 shaped the original rule): a Sky item that only ONE class's tests want now checks off for that class no matter which tab or class filter is active — a Berserker-only staff looted on the Druid tab is still Berserker progress. Shared items (the runes several classes need) keep respecting your class filter, because one physical rune can't honestly tick five class plans.

THE BIG ONE — everything since 1.60 lands together: the ⧗ fight timeline, the 🐌 slow alert with cures attached, ⏳ buff timers that learn your real durations, 🐉 raid-target tracking, level & AA progress charts, per-skill miss rates and hit ranges, both DPS models labeled, rules from recent log lines, watch sorting, a minimize hotkey, tabbed Options, and a reorganized ⚙ menu. Scroll back through the entries below for each one's story.

EQBuddy is a BETA and this update is enormous — if a number looks wrong, a timer runs long, a card confuses you, or you simply wish it did something else: tell us in GitHub Discussions (⚙ → Help → Send feedback). Nearly everything in this update exists because somebody did exactly that.

The ⚙ gear menu got the same treatment as Options: your windows up top (map, travel, quests, spawns, inventory, history, drops), the two in-play actions (camp marker, click-through), and everything else shelved under Data & imports and Help. Set-and-forget toggles — track spawns, grid overlay, cursor ring — now live in Options tabs where settings belong (cursor ring: Look tab).

Options grew tabs — Look · Alerts & chips · Watch rules · Cards & windows · Behavior — instead of one long wall (David: “it needs serious reorganization”; he was right). Opens to the tab you last used.

Buff timers got smarter: your own casts now include your Spell Casting Reinforcement rank (+5/15/30/50%) straight from your AA ledger, and a new display mode (Alerts & chips tab) keeps the card quiet until a buff is within a warning window you choose — tell me when it matters.
The voice no longer arrives late to its own alert: the speech engine warms up at launch, so the first spoken alert of a session speaks on time.

Cards you haven’t hidden now ALWAYS show — what you select in Options is what the widget displays, automatically. A card with nothing yet (Buffs before a buff lands, Raids before a kill, Watch before your first rule) shows one honest line saying what will fill it, instead of hiding and reading as a missing feature. The widget grows on its own as cards fill; the bottom grip is only for choosing a SHORTER widget (double-click returns to automatic).

The widget's bottom-edge grip now says what a drag can do right now — with every card already visible there is nothing more to reveal (cards marked · auto appear when they have content), and a control that silently no-ops reads as broken.

Polish from the first field test (thanks, David): new cards now slot into the MIDDLE of your card order instead of hiding below the fold; self-hiding cards (Watch, Buffs, Raids) say "· auto" in Options with a tooltip explaining when they appear; the bottom-edge height grip is twice as grabbable and glows when you find it; the hotkey recorder now TELLS you a bare key needs Ctrl/Alt/Shift instead of silently ignoring it (and ✕ unbinds); and the recent-lines rule picker grew a "hide chat" filter for when General channel drowns your combat lines.

NEW: 🐉 Raids card — every raid target from the game's own achievements list, per zone, with YOUR record: kills your log witnessed (with dates — a kill counts because you were there, whoever landed the blow), plus clears from before EQBuddy via the achievements import. No difficulty-tier badges yet, deliberately: neither the log nor the dump names the instance tier, and we won't decorate what the data can't back — if you know a log line that reveals the tier, tell us!

A reminder as these features pour in: EQBuddy is a BETA. Every card, timer and number in it got better because someone spoke up — keep the feedback and suggestions coming in GitHub Discussions, rough edges and wild ideas alike.

NEW: buff timers — a ⏳ Buffs card counts down every buff on you, soonest-fading first. Timers start from your own casts OR someone else's cast landing on you, run on wiki durations labeled "est", and LEARN your real durations from natural fades (ranks and AAs lengthen buffs — after one full cycle the est drops and the number is yours). Buffs survive zoning, clear on death, and the card hides itself when you have none. 263 buffs built in.

NEW: character progress charts in Session History — pick a character and see Level over time (every ding, exact times, a staircase not a slope) and AA earned over time (cumulative), mined from the sessions you already have.

NEW: "+ From a recent log line…" in Options → watch rules — pick any line that just happened in your log and it becomes a Text rule instantly, match prefilled, ready to trim. Nobody should have to remember a log line to watch for it.
The Tracked card learned to sort (discussion #105, thanks wizen): manual / a–z / total / recent links on the card, and ▲▼ arrows in Options arrange the manual order.
New hotkey action (discussion #100, thanks jlcrisp): minimize / restore the dashboard — bind it under Options → Global hotkeys.

Breakdown rows learned their misses: melee rows now show an inline miss % ("14% miss", out of attempts — hover for the raw count), and every row's tooltip carries the hit range ("hits 88–412"). Works on the Combat card, the breakout windows, and per-fight views alike.

The Combat card now states BOTH session DPS models, labeled: "Session dps: 412 in combat · 267 wall-clock" — in-combat is the honest camp number (medding doesn't dilute it), wall-clock is what the whole session actually produced. Pick the one that matches your question.

NEW: the fight timeline — click ⧗ on the Combat card (or the floating Damage window) and see the whole pull on one canvas: a lane per skill, every hit as a bar (taller = harder, orange = critical), every miss and resist as a hollow outline with the log's own words on hover ("a gnoll pup ripostes"), your pet and the incoming damage in their own lanes, and a DPS-over-time graph on top with the peak flagged. Scroll to zoom around your cursor, drag to pan, Fit snaps back to the whole fight — and a live fight keeps drawing itself onto the canvas as you play.
Miss lines now carry their attack skill through the parser, so the timeline (and everything after it) knows a missed backstab from a missed kick.

NEW: slow alert (discussion #94, thanks Frankthetankk) — when an attack-speed debuff lands on you, a 🐌 chip appears with the slow's % and counter count ("Slowed 40% · 12 disease counters"), an optional voice announces it once, and the chip clears when the debuff fades or runs out. Hover the chip for the cure line, strongest first ("Abolish Disease removes 36/cast"). Built in for all 34 known slows — no per-spell setup. When several slows share a landing line, the chip shows the honest range ("Slowed 23–75%") instead of guessing. Options has the off-switch, the voice toggle, and a raids-only mode (detected from raid-channel chat).

macOS players, this one's yours — contributed by quasarj (PR #103): EQBuddy's windows now stay ABOVE the game when EQ Legends runs fullscreen under CrossOver/Wine, instead of vanishing behind it. The raise only kicks in while the game is frontmost, so EQBuddy doesn't float over your other apps.
The Options window can finally be resized on macOS and Linux: drag either side edge, same invisible grips as on Windows, and the width you pick is remembered (also quasarj, PR #103).

FIXED: clicking the ⚡ (or 🐾) glyph next to its star in the Combat header collapsed the section instead of toggling the mini-dashboard chip — the glyph now toggles the star it belongs to (David's live catch, minutes after 1.59.0).

The minimized DPS card learned two asks from discussion #102 (thanks jeremycranfill): a ⧉ button on its header copies the last fight as Discord-ready text without leaving the minimized view, and session-scope spell rows now show a resist % — "do I need to switch to overchannel?" answered where you're already looking. The % is your own casts vs. resists this session (hover for the raw counts); the main Combat card's session rows carry it too.
New ⚡ star in the Combat section header: an optional proc-rate chip (procs per combat-minute, same honest denominator as the Procs card) for the mini dashboard.

The big chains are now real quests, step by step: Coldain Ring #1–#9 (the 10th already had its own page), all seven Prayer Shawls, the deity Symbol chains, and every class armor set (Kael, Skyshrine, Thurgadin, Darkforge, Dreadscale, Trooper Scale, Ivy Etched, Lambent, Totemic, and more) — 250 per-step quests split out of the wiki's chain pages. The quest tracker's "held" tab now shows everything your inventory is GOOD FOR, not just what's finished: "Ready from your bags" leads, then "Your bags contribute" — every quest your items partly cover, sorted by how close you are. And the /outputfile inventory reminder became a button: click ⧉ copy, paste into the game's chat, done — the game writes the file, EQBuddy reads it, and everything you loot afterward counts on top automatically.

FIXED: clicking a quest item's 🗺 badge could say "nothing matches" when the quest belonged to a class outside your class filter — Blue Orc Head leads to The Falchion (Paladin), and a BRD/MNK/WAR filter silently erased it (David's live catch in Crushbone). Search now ALWAYS answers with the whole catalog — class, era, and state filters shape the browse tabs, never the search — and each result card states whose quest it is. A new permanent test walks every turn-in item in the catalog through the real search to prove the badge's promise can't break again. The Quest Tracker also widened so the search box can't be squeezed invisible by the filter row.

If you imported before this fix and your primary class got false checkmarks: untick those reward checkboxes on the Sky card and they stay honest.

Two Reddit asks, same day: mez countdown chips can now be turned OFF (⚙ Options — untick and the stack never appears; a class that never mezzes never wanted it), and the Progress card stops reciting your entire AA history — "AA learned this session" shows what's new, and the full ledger folds behind an "▸ All AA abilities" click, exactly like Pet abilities.

Section headlines and item-page links now use the RESOLVED wiki title, so "a decaying skeleton" is no longer suggested as "Decaying skeleton" — and new-page instructions say to keep the a/an/the the log reader strips.

Each now splits into real per-test quests — "Wizard Sky Test: Nargon's Staff" with just that test's items and NPC — class-scoped, era-tagged, and finally in agreement with the Sky checklist card. The held/ready/done filters mean something per test now.

The epics keep their honest 40-item lists; they really are one quest.

Bind show/hide-everything, the zone map, quest tracker, spawn timers, or click-through. 📊 The widget opens with a KPI strip — dps · kills · loot · xp/hr, always visible — and the Combat card finally DRAWS the damage timeline it's been recording all along: a damage-per-minute sparkline for your last half hour, hottest minute marked, quiet minutes honestly flat.

Every window came along: the breakouts, Quest Tracker, Sky checklist (compact class chips), Inventory, Spawns, Options. Not one feature moved. If your hands know EQBuddy, they still do — it just stopped dressing like a spreadsheet.

Pairs with the inventory import, which can mark pieces you banked long ago.

And the Plane of Sky checklist now floats your UNFINISHED quests to the top of each class tab, with each quest's still-missing items listed first — down to 1-2 left per class, the things you keep forgetting are now the first things you see. Completed quests sink to the bottom as trophies.

🎒 YOUR BAGS, IN THE WIDGET: type /outputfile inventory in game and EQBuddy reads the file the game writes — right-click → Inventory… shows your worn gear by slot and what's in every bag, and the quest tracker grows a "held" tab: quests whose ENTIRE turn-in list your bags already cover. Better still, the log keeps it current — loot something and the counts update live, with a "Looted since this dump" section so the view stays honest about what the dump knows versus what the log saw. Plane of Sky planning just got a lot shorter.

⧉ Share a parse (jeremycranfill's ask, #89): the Combat card's Last fight line grows a copy button — one click puts the fight on your clipboard as a Discord-ready monospace block, abilities aligned with percentages, pet rows labeled in. 🎭 EQBuddy infers your class from your most-used class-unique skills (Backstab, Harm Touch, the monk kicks, bard songs…) and pre-filters the quest tracker with it when you haven't picked classes — always labeled "(inferred)", never persisted, and one pick in the class filter overrides it. Clickies lose the vote by volume.

📐 Windows behave (badly-developed's asks, #95/#96): chip stacks can GROW UPWARD (Options — anchored at their bottom edge, so boss timers sit above mez timers with each growing away from the other), and breakout windows now follow the main widget's background see-through. The wiki contribution pack folds upgrade tiers into one entry (Frankthetankk's catch, #65) — no more identical duplicate lines when base and +1 both dropped.

You're often the first person to see a drop; a minute of pasting makes every EQBuddy user's tracker smarter.

Quest items the wiki half-remembers count anyway (wizen's Phosphorous Powder, #75): some item pages say QUEST ITEM right in the stats block but miss the category tag the tracker reads. The page's own flag counts now — look an item up once and its 🗺 badge appears, category or no category. Race unlocks shouldn't hinge on a wiki editor's bookkeeping.

Getting maps is one click now: the map window grew a "Get maps…" button that opens Brewall's EverQuest Maps (eqmaps.info) — a quarter century of cartography, and the reason the Zone map has something beautiful to draw.
